A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on MMRole and PCogAlignBench, including benchmark performance, component ablations, rollout diversity, timing, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds codebook-size evaluation in Appendix C.1 and Table 5.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, model components, training objectives, and inference procedures are unchanged. The added Section 3.3 explanation about freezing the world model and optimizing one latent action per response token clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: The training corpora and evaluated tasks remain unchanged: MMRole Comment with ID/OOD evaluation and PCogAlignBench with LS1/LS2 evaluation. Newly cited traditional dialogue benchmarks are discussed rather than evaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Prompt, SFT, and token-level versus latent-action GRPO, Dr.GRPO, DAPO, and BNPO. The component-ablation and data-exposure comparators are also retained.

E3.justification: The new Appendix C.1 experiment evaluates codebook sizes 64 and 256 alongside the retained default of 128, using Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct and GRPO. Existing splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets, and inference settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 and Table 5 add a sensitivity analysis testing whether performance depends on codebook size. Existing component ablations, data-exposure controls, computational analysis, and case studies remain.

E5.justification: Section 4.4 now specifies five independent runs and standard deviations across seeds for rollout diversity. v1 described averaging over training samples without identifying the run/seed basis of Table 3's uncertainty. This establishes newly specified reporting, not an increase from a known earlier run count; main benchmark evaluation still uses three runs.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises diversity estimates under the newly specified statistical reporting; for example, MMRole GRPO (Latent Action) changes from 1.256 ± 0.302 to 1.248 ± 0.002. New Table 5 adds average scores of 0.896 and 0.897 for sizes 64 and 256 alongside the retained 128 result of 0.893. Tables 1-2 and the retained appendix performance results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, objectives in Equations 1-9, diversity formula in Equation 10, and Appendix A mathematics are unchanged. The new sequence-length explanation restates consequences of the existing procedure rather than introducing new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about compact latent actions, the cross-modal projector with cycle consistency, and improvements on two conversational tasks.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new size sweep as evidence of robustness and adds a long-response rationale for benchmark selection. It newly acknowledges latent-action interpretability and larger-model validation limitations, and replaces v1's blanket no-negative-impact statement with specific discussion of persona coverage, role-set bias, and stereotypes.

D1.justification: The abstract adds an explicit repository link for code and data. Architectural details, training hyperparameters, hardware, evaluation prompts, and decoding settings in Appendices A-B remain unchanged; the PDFs alone do not verify the linked resources.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to PhotoBook, GuessWhat?!, Visual Dialog, and Feng et al. (2025) to motivate benchmark selection through response length and exploration difficulty. The central positioning relative to CoLA and other latent-action research is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 corrects codebook typos and the unresolved TRL citation, adds targeted methodological and benchmark explanations, expands limitations, rewrites Ethics Considerations, and adds acknowledgments and an appendix subsection. The overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds codebook-size Table 5 and relocates existing displays, including Algorithm 1, Figure 4, and the main result tables. Existing diagrams, plots, case-study figures, and table formats are preserved; subsequent appendix tables are renumbered.

improvement.justification: The new codebook-size analysis provides limited robustness evidence, and the five-run diversity description makes uncertainty reporting more interpretable. Explicit interpretability and persona-bias limitations improve qualification of the work, while the code/data link improves access information. These are useful, bounded improvements; the core method and main benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
